page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a performance profile centered in the average tier for multi-core operations, while single-core performance leans toward the weaker tier. Specifically, the stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression are categorized in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores, consistently fall within the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, as well as Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, also demonstrate average performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides a high density of dedicated compute resources relative to memory, making it suitable for workloads that require parallel processing but have moderate memory footprints. The lack of bundled local storage means storage-heavy applications will require external block storage attachments. This server is best suited for workloads such as multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, and database operations that can leverage its 32 dedicated vCPUs without requiring high single-core clock speeds or GPU acceleration.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor at 2.5 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Performance benchmarks place the instance in the average tier for multi-core operations, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU tests, though single-core performance is weaker, falling in the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core and gzip compression. This resource profile offers a balanced cost-to-compute ratio for parallel workloads. It is best suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, web serving, and database operations that do not require high single-core performance or local NVMe storage.
